text_mt: "Speech is joined with breath," says Kauṇṭharavya, "breath with the purifying [wind], the purifying [wind] with the All-gods, the All-gods with the heavenly world, the heavenly world with Brahman. This is the continuous text (saṃhitā) linked from lower to higher." He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) linked from lower to higher is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world, just as this continuous text (saṃhitā) is linked from lower to higher. If, having been addressed by another or on his own business, he speaks, he should know as he speaks: "The continuous text (saṃhitā) has gone to heaven, for the purpose of the wise gods speaking; so shall it be." By this [continuous text] linked from lower to higher, it truly happens in that way.

sanskrit_iast: mātā pūrvarūpaṃ pitottararūpaṃ prajā saṃhiteti bhārgavaḥ | tad etad ekam eva sarvaṃ abhyanūktam | mātā ca hyevedaṃ pitā ca prajā ca sarvam | saiṣāditisaṃhitā | aditir hevedaṃ sarvaṃ yad idaṃ kiṃcid viśvabhūtam | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam aditir dyaur aditir antarikṣaṃ aditir mātā sā pitā sa putraḥ | viśve devā aditiḥ pañca janā aditir jātam aditir janitvam || sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: माता पूर्वरूपं पितोत्तररूपं प्रजा संहितेति भार्गवः | तद् एतद् एकम् एव सर्वं अभ्यनूक्तम् | माता च ह्येवेदं पिता च प्रजा च सर्वम् | सैषादितिसंहिता | अदितिर् हेवेदं सर्वं यद् इदं किंचिद् विश्वभूतम् | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् अदितिर् द्यौर् अदितिर् अन्तरिक्षं अदितिर् माता सा पिता स पुत्रः | विश्वे देवा अदितिः पञ्च जना अदितिर् जातम् अदितिर् जनित्वम् || स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: The mother is the form of the former, the father of the latter. The child is the union,' sa3's Bhargava. All that is declared to be one. For the mother and the father and the child are this all. This is the Aditi union. For Aditi is this all, whatever this universe is. This is declared in a Re:—5 'Aditi is the heaven, Aditi atmosphere, Aditi is the mother, the father, and the son, Aditi is all gods, Aditi the five races, Aditi all that hath been born and shall be born.' He who knows thus this union is united with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: "The mother is the first member, the father the second member, offspring the continuous text (saṃhitā)," says Bhārgava. This whole [universe] is referred to as one alone; for mother, father, and offspring are this all. This is the Aditi-saṃhitā. For Aditi is all this, whatever exists here as all creation. This has been declared by the Ṛgvedic verse: / 'Aditi is heaven, Aditi is the intermediate space, / Aditi is mother, father, and son. / Aditi is all the gods, the five peoples; / Aditi is what is born, Aditi is what is to be born.' / He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: jāyā pūrvarūpaṃ patir uttararūpaṃ putraḥ saṃhitā retaḥ saṃdhiḥ prajananaṃ saṃdhānam iti sthaviraḥ śākalyaḥ | saiṣā prajāpatisaṃhitā | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: जाया पूर्वरूपं पतिर् उत्तररूपं पुत्रः संहिता रेतः संधिः प्रजननं संधानम् इति स्थविरः शाकल्यः | सैषा प्रजापतिसंहिता | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: The wife is the symbol of the former, the husband of the latter. The son is the union, the seed the joining, the begetting the joiner,' says Sthavira Sakalya. This is the Prajiipati union. He who knows thus this union is increased " with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: "The wife is the first member, the husband the second member, the son the continuous text (saṃhitā), semen the junction, procreation the joining," says the elder Śākalya. This is the Prajāpati-saṃhitā. He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: prajñā pūrvarūpaṃ śraddhottararūpaṃ karma saṃhitā satyaṃ saṃdhānam iti kāśyapaḥ | saiṣā satyasaṃhitā | tad āhur yat satyasaṃdhā devā iti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: प्रज्ञा पूर्वरूपं श्रद्धोत्तररूपं कर्म संहिता सत्यं संधानम् इति काश्यपः | सैषा सत्यसंहिता | तद् आहुर् यत् सत्यसंधा देवा इति | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: Offspring is the symbol of the former, faith of the latter. Action is the union, truth the joiner,' says Kasyapa. This is the truth union. They say the gods are of true unions. He who knows thus this union is united with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: "Insight is the first member, faith the second member, action the continuous text (saṃhitā), truth the joining," says Kāśyapa. This is the Satya-saṃhitā. Thus they say: "The gods are true to their word (satyasaṃdha)." He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: vāk saṃhiteti pañcālacaṇḍaḥ | vācā vai vedāḥ saṃdhīyante vācā chandāṃsi vācā mitrāṇi saṃdadhati | tad yatraitad adhīte vā bhāṣate vā vāci tadā prāṇo bhavati | vāk tadā prāṇaṃ reḷhi | atha yat svapiti vā tūṣṇīṃ vā bhavati prāṇe tadā vāg bhavati prāṇastadā vācaṃ reḷhi | tāv anyonyaṃ rīḷhaḥ | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ekaḥ suparṇaḥ sa samudram āviveśa, sa idaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ vicaṣṭe | taṃ pākena manasāpaśyam antitas, taṃ mātā reḷhi sa u reḷhi mātaram || iti | vāg vai mātā prāṇo vatsaḥ | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: वाक् संहितेति पञ्चालचण्डः | वाचा वै वेदाः संधीयन्ते वाचा छन्दांसि वाचा मित्राणि संदधति | तद् यत्रैतद् अधीते वा भाषते वा वाचि तदा प्राणो भवति | वाक् तदा प्राणं रेऌहि | अथ यत् स्वपिति वा तूष्णीं वा भवति प्राणे तदा वाग् भवति प्राणस्तदा वाचं रेऌहि | ताव् अन्योन्यं रीऌहः | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् एकः सुपर्णः स समुद्रम् आविवेश, स इदं विश्वं भुवनं विचष्टे | तं पाकेन मनसापश्यम् अन्तितस्, तं माता रेऌहि स उ रेऌहि मातरम् || इति | वाग् वै माता प्राणो वत्सः | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: Speech is the union,' says Pancalacanda. By speech, indeed, the Vedas are united, by speech the metres, by speech he unites friends. "When he studies or speaks, then breath is in speech, then speech absorbs breath. Again, when he sleeps or is silent, then speech is in breath, then breath absorbs speech; they absorb each other. This is declared in a Re:—5 'One of these birds hath passed into the sea of air; thence he looks round and views this universal world. With simple heart I have beheld him close at hand; his mother him absorbs, and her he too absorbs.' Speech, indeed, is the mother, breath the child. He who knows thus this union is united with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: "Speech is the continuous text (saṃhitā)," says Pañcālacaṇḍa. "By speech the Vedas are joined; by speech the metres; by speech they unite friends. Then, when one studies or speaks, breath is then in speech; speech then licks breath. But when one sleeps or is silent, speech is then in breath; breath then licks speech. They lick each other." This has been declared by the Ṛgvedic verse: / 'One fair-winged bird entered the ocean; / he surveys this whole world. / With an innocent mind I saw him close at hand; / his mother licks him, and he licks his mother.' / Speech indeed is the mother; breath is the calf. He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: bṛhadrathaṃtareṇa rūpeṇa saṃhitā saṃdhīyata iti tārkṣyaḥ | vāg vai rathaṃtarasya rūpaṃ prāṇo bṛhataḥ | ubhābhyām u khalu saṃhitā saṃdhīyate vācā ca prāṇena ca | etasyāṃ ha smopaniṣadi saṃvatsaraṃ gā rakṣayata iti tārkṣyaḥ | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: बृहद्रथंतरेण रूपेण संहिता संधीयत इति तार्क्ष्यः | वाग् वै रथंतरस्य रूपं प्राणो बृहतः | उभाभ्याम् उ खलु संहिता संधीयते वाचा च प्राणेन च | एतस्यां ह स्मोपनिषदि संवत्सरं गा रक्षयत इति तार्क्ष्यः | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: The union is made by the symbol of Brhat and Rathantara,' says Tarksya. Speech, indeed, is the symbol of the Rathantara, breath of the Brhat. By both, indeed, is the union made, by speech and breath. For the sake of this Upaniṣad one watches cows for a year,' says Tarksya. 'For the sake of just this one watches cows for a year,' says Tarksya. He who knows thus this union is imited with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: "Through the form of Bṛhat and Rathantara the continuous text (saṃhitā) is joined," says Tārkṣya. "Speech indeed is the form of Rathantara, breath of Bṛhat. And by both indeed is the continuous text (saṃhitā) joined—by speech and by breath." In this secret teaching (upaniṣad) [the teacher] had him guard the cows for a year: so says Tārkṣya. He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: gatiḥ pūrvvarūpaṃ nivṛttir uttararūpaṃ sthitiḥ saṃhiteti jāratkārava ārtabhāgaḥ | tasyām etasyāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ dhvaṃsayo nimeṣāḥ kāṣṭhāḥ kalāḥ kṣaṇā muhūrtā ahorātrā ardhamāsā māsā ṛtavaḥ saṃvatsarāś ca saṃdhīyante | saiṣā saṃhitainān kālān saṃdadhāti | kālo gatinivṛttisthitīḥ saṃdadhāti | gatinivṛttisthitibhir idaṃ sarvaṃ saṃdhīyate | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam bhūtaṃ pūrvarūpaṃ bhaviṣyad uttararūpaṃ bhavat saṃhiteti kālasaṃdhiḥ | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam mahat tan nāma guhyaṃ puruspṛg yena bhutaṃ janayo yena bhavyam | pratnaṃ jātaṃ jyotir yad asya priyaṃ priyāḥ samaviśanta pañca || iti | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: गतिः पूर्व्वरूपं निवृत्तिर् उत्तररूपं स्थितिः संहितेति जारत्कारव आर्तभागः | तस्याम् एतस्यां संहितायां ध्वंसयो निमेषाः काष्ठाः कलाः क्षणा मुहूर्ता अहोरात्रा अर्धमासा मासा ऋतवः संवत्सराश् च संधीयन्ते | सैषा संहितैनान् कालान् संदधाति | कालो गतिनिवृत्तिस्थितीः संदधाति | गतिनिवृत्तिस्थितिभिर् इदं सर्वं संधीयते | इत्यधिदैवतम् | अथाध्यात्मम् भूतं पूर्वरूपं भविष्यद् उत्तररूपं भवत् संहितेति कालसंधिः | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् महत् तन् नाम गुह्यं पुरुस्पृग् येन भुतं जनयो येन भव्यम् | प्रत्नं जातं ज्योतिर् यद् अस्य प्रियं प्रियाः समविशन्त पञ्च || इति | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: Movement is the symbol of the former, stopping of the latter. Rest is the union,' says Jaratkiirava Artabhaga. In this union there are united dhvamsk, nimesas, kastfids, seconds, minutes, hours, days and nights, half-months, months, seasons, and years. This union unites these times; time unites movement, stopping, and rest. By movement, stopping, and rest, all this is united. So far as regards the deities. Now as regards the self. The past is the symbol of the former, the future of the latter. The present is the union. This is the time union. This is declared in a Re:— * * Great is that secret name, and far extending, whereby thou madest all present and future. The light he loveth that was made aforetime, the five tribes whom he loveth well have entered.' He who knows thus this union is united with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: "Motion is the first member, cessation the second member, rest the continuous text (saṃhitā)," says Jāratkārava Ārtabhāga. In this continuous text (saṃhitā), sparks, winks, kāṣṭhās, kalās, moments, muhūrtas, days and nights, fortnights, months, seasons, and years are joined together. This continuous text (saṃhitā) joins these divisions of time. Time joins motion, cessation, and rest. By motion, cessation, and rest, this all is joined together. Thus with respect to the deities. Now with respect to the self: "The past is the first member, the future the second member, the present the continuous text (saṃhitā)"—such is the junction of time. This has been declared by the Ṛgvedic verse: / 'Great is that secret name, much-desired, / by which thou didst generate the past, by which the future. / An ancient light was born which was dear to him; / the five dear [peoples] entered into it.' / He who knows this continuous text (saṃhitā) thus is joined with offspring, cattle, fame, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: athāto vāliśikhāyaner vacaḥ | pañcemāni mahābhūtāni bhavantīti ha smāha vāliśikhayaniḥ | pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyautīṃṣi tāni mithaḥ saṃhitani bhavanti | aatha yānyanyāni kṣudrāṇi mahābhūtaiḥ saṃdhīyante saiṣā sarvavibhūtasaṃhitā | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: अथातो वालिशिखायनेर् वचः | पञ्चेमानि महाभूतानि भवन्तीति ह स्माह वालिशिखयनिः | पृथिवी वायुर् आकाशम् आपो ज्यौतींषि तानि मिथः संहितनि भवन्ति | अअथ यान्यन्यानि क्षुद्राणि महाभूतैः संधीयन्ते सैषा सर्वविभूतसंहिता | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: Then follows the saying of Valisikhayani. 'There are, then, five gross elements,' says Valisikhayani, 'the earth, wind, ether, water, light. These are united with each other. Again, the others, the small ones, are united with the gross elements. This is the union of all elements. He who knows thus this union is united with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days.
text_mt: Now then, the teaching of Vāliśikhāyani. “These are the five gross elements,” Vāliśikhāyani used to say: “earth, wind, space, waters, luminaries; these are continuous with one another. And the others, which are lesser, are joined with the gross elements. That is the continuous text of all powers. He who knows this continuous text thus is joined with offspring, cattle, renown, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he attains a complete lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: sarvā vāg brahmeti ha smāha lauhikyaḥ | ye tu kecana śabdā vācam eva tāṃ vidyāt | tad apyetad ṛṣir āha ahaṃ rudrebhir vasubhiś carāmīti | saiṣā vāk sarvaśabdā bhavati | sa ya evam etāṃ saṃhitāṃ veda saṃdhīyate prajayā paśubhir yaśasā brahmavarcasena svargeṇa lokena sarvam āyur eti | yatā caitad brahma kāmarūpi kāmacāri bhavatyevaṃ haiva sa sarveṣu bhūteṣu kāmarūpī kāmacārī bhavati | ya evaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: सर्वा वाग् ब्रह्मेति ह स्माह लौहिक्यः | ये तु केचन शब्दा वाचम् एव तां विद्यात् | तद् अप्येतद् ऋषिर् आह अहं रुद्रेभिर् वसुभिश् चरामीति | सैषा वाक् सर्वशब्दा भवति | स य एवम् एतां संहितां वेद संधीयते प्रजया पशुभिर् यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेन स्वर्गेण लोकेन सर्वम् आयुर् एति | यता चैतद् ब्रह्म कामरूपि कामचारि भवत्येवं हैव स सर्वेषु भूतेषु कामरूपी कामचारी भवति | य एवं वेद य एवं वेद ||
text: The whole of speech is Brahman,' says Lauhikya. Whatever sounds there are, let him know to be sjDcech. This a Rsi declares:—^ 'I with the Rudras and the Yasus fare.' This speech is all sounds. He who knows thus this union is united with children, cattle, glory, holiness, the world of heaven. He lives all his days. And even as Brahman(n.) can change form at will and move at will, so among all beings can he change form and move at will who knows thus.
text_mt: "All speech is Brahman," Lauhikya used to say. Whatever sounds there are, one should know them as just speech. Regarding this, the ṛṣi also says: "I move with the Rudras and the Vasus..." This speech consists of all sounds. He who thus knows this continuous text is joined with offspring, cattle, renown, brahminical splendour, and the heavenly world; he reaches a full lifespan. And just as this Brahman can take any form at will and move at will, even so he can take any form at will and move at will among all beings—he who knows thus, he who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo vaṃśa iti ha smāha sthaviraḥ śākalyaḥ | tadu yathā śālāvaṃśe sarve 'nye vaṃśāḥ samāhitāḥ syur evam evaitasmin prāṇe sarva ātmā samāhitaḥ | tasyaitadyātmanaḥ prāṇa ūṣmarūpam asthīni sparśarūpaṃ majjānaḥ svararūpaṃ māṃsaṃ lohitam ityetac caturtham antasthārūpam iti | treyaṃ tveva na etat proktam iti ha smāha hvastro māṇḍūkeyaḥ | tasyaitasya trayasya trīṇītaḥ ṣaṣṭiśatāni bhavanti saṃdhīnāṃ trīṇītas tāni saptaviṃśatiśatāni bhavanti | sapta vai viṃśatiśatāni saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇām | tat saṃvatsarasyāhorātrāṇyāpnoti | sa eṣa saṃvatsarasaṃmānaś cakṣurmayaś śrotramayaś chandomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā | sa ya evam etaṃ saṃvatsarasaṃmānaṃ cakṣurmayaṃ śrotramayaṃ chandomayaṃ manomayaṃ vāmayam ātmānaṃ veda saṃvatsarasya sāyaujyaṃ salokatāṃ sarūpatāṃ sabhakṣatām aśnute | putrī paśumān bhavati sarvam āyur etyasyāruṇikeyo devayāñcakre ||
meaning: प्राणो वंश इति ह स्माह स्थविरः शाकल्यः | तदु यथा शालावंशे सर्वे ऽन्ये वंशाः समाहिताः स्युर् एवम् एवैतस्मिन् प्राणे सर्व आत्मा समाहितः | तस्यैतद्यात्मनः प्राण ऊष्मरूपम् अस्थीनि स्पर्शरूपं मज्जानः स्वररूपं मांसं लोहितम् इत्येतच् चतुर्थम् अन्तस्थारूपम् इति | त्रेयं त्वेव न एतत् प्रोक्तम् इति ह स्माह ह्वस्त्रो माण्डूकेयः | तस्यैतस्य त्रयस्य त्रीणीतः षष्टिशतानि भवन्ति संधीनां त्रीणीतस् तानि सप्तविंशतिशतानि भवन्ति | सप्त वै विंशतिशतानि संवत्सरस्याहोरात्राणाम् | तत् संवत्सरस्याहोरात्राण्याप्नोति | स एष संवत्सरसंमानश् चक्षुर्मयश् श्रोत्रमयश् छन्दोमयो मनोमयो वाङ्मय आत्मा | स य एवम् एतं संवत्सरसंमानं चक्षुर्मयं श्रोत्रमयं छन्दोमयं मनोमयं वामयम् आत्मानं वेद संवत्सरस्य सायौज्यं सलोकतां सरूपतां सभक्षताम् अश्नुते | पुत्री पशुमान् भवति सर्वम् आयुर् एत्यस्यारुणिकेयो देवयाञ्चक्रे ||
text: Om. 'Breath is the beam,' says Sthavira Siikalya. 'Just as all the other beams rest on the main-beam, so the whole self rests on this breath. Of this self breath is the symbol of the sibilants, the bones of the mutes, the marrow of the vowels, the flesh and blood, the fourth element, of the semi-vowels.' 'But we have heard of a triad only,' says Hrasva Mandukeya. Of this triad, on one side there are three hundred and sixty joinings, on the other the.same; these make up seven hundred and twenty. Seven hundred and twenty, indeed, are the days and nights of the year. Thus he obtains the days and nights of the year. This is the self, commensurate with the year, composed of the eye, the ear, the metres, the mind, speech. He who knows thus this self, commensurate with the year, composed of the eye, the ear, the metres, the mind, speech, wins union, and communion with the year, residence in the same world, and similarity of form. He becomes rich in sons and cattle. He lives all his days. So taught Arunikeya.
text_mt: "Breath is the beam," old Śākalya used to say. Just as all the other beams are set upon the central ridge-beam of a house, even so this entire self is set upon this breath. Of this self, breath is the form of the sibilants, bones of the stops, marrow of the vowels, and the fourth, flesh and blood, is the form of the semivowels. "Only this threefold [division] was proclaimed, not that [fourfold one]," Hvastra Māṇḍūkeya used to say. Of this threefold [division], there are three hundred and sixty junctions here, and three hundred and sixty there; they become twenty-seven hundred. Twenty-seven hundred indeed are the days and nights of a year. Thereby he obtains the days and nights of the year. This same self is the measure of the year, consisting of sight, consisting of hearing, consisting of metre, consisting of mind, consisting of speech. He who thus knows this self, which is the measure of the year, consisting of sight, consisting of hearing, consisting of metre, consisting of mind, consisting of speech, attains union with the year, dwelling in the same world, having the same form, and sharing the same food. He becomes possessed of sons, possessed of cattle; he reaches a full lifespan. To him [the son of] Āruṇi made divine offering.

sanskrit_iast: atha kauṣṭharavyaḥ | trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatānyakṣarāṇām | trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatānyūṣmaṇām | trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatāni saṃdhīnām | yānyakṣarāṇyavocāmāhāni tāni | yān ūṣmaṇo rātrayastāḥ | yān saṃdhīn avocāmāhorātrāṇāṃ te saṃdhayaḥ | ityadhidaivatam | athādhyātmam yānyakṣarāṇyadhidaivatam avocāmāsthīni tānyadhyātmam | yān ūṣmaṇo 'dhidaivatam avocāma majjānas te 'dhyātmam | eṣa u ha vai saṃpratiprāṇo yan majjā etad retaḥ na vā ṛte prāṇād retasaḥ siddhir asti | yad vā ṛte prāṇād retaḥ sicyeta tat pūyen na saṃbhavet | yān saṃdhīn adhidaivatam avocāma parvāṇi tānyadhyātmam | tasyaitasyāsthnāṃ majjā parvaṇām iti pañcetaścatvāriṃśacchatāni bhavanti | saṃdhīnāṃ pañcetastadaśītisahasraṃ bhavati | aśītisahasraṃ vārkalino bṛhatīr aharahani saṃpādayanti | sa eṣo 'haḥsaṃmānaś cakṣurmayaś śrotramayaś chandomayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā | sa ya evam etad ahaḥsaṃmānaṃ cakṣurmayaṃ śrotramayaṃ chandomayaṃ manomayaṃ vāmayam ātmānaṃ veda ahnāṃ sāyaujyaṃ salokatāṃ sarūpatāṃ sabhakṣatām aśnute | putrī paśumān bhavati sarvam āyur eti ||
meaning: अथ कौष्ठरव्यः | त्रीणि षष्टिशतान्यक्षराणाम् | त्रीणि षष्टिशतान्यूष्मणाम् | त्रीणि षष्टिशतानि संधीनाम् | यान्यक्षराण्यवोचामाहानि तानि | यान् ऊष्मणो रात्रयस्ताः | यान् संधीन् अवोचामाहोरात्राणां ते संधयः | इत्यधिदैवतम् | अथाध्यात्मम् यान्यक्षराण्यधिदैवतम् अवोचामास्थीनि तान्यध्यात्मम् | यान् ऊष्मणो ऽधिदैवतम् अवोचाम मज्जानस् ते ऽध्यात्मम् | एष उ ह वै संप्रतिप्राणो यन् मज्जा एतद् रेतः न वा ऋते प्राणाद् रेतसः सिद्धिर् अस्ति | यद् वा ऋते प्राणाद् रेतः सिच्येत तत् पूयेन् न संभवेत् | यान् संधीन् अधिदैवतम् अवोचाम पर्वाणि तान्यध्यात्मम् | तस्यैतस्यास्थ्नां मज्जा पर्वणाम् इति पञ्चेतश्चत्वारिंशच्छतानि भवन्ति | संधीनां पञ्चेतस्तदशीतिसहस्रं भवति | अशीतिसहस्रं वार्कलिनो बृहतीर् अहरहनि संपादयन्ति | स एषो ऽहःसंमानश् चक्षुर्मयश् श्रोत्रमयश् छन्दोमयो मनोमयो वाङ्मय आत्मा | स य एवम् एतद् अहःसंमानं चक्षुर्मयं श्रोत्रमयं छन्दोमयं मनोमयं वामयम् आत्मानं वेद अह्नां सायौज्यं सलोकतां सरूपतां सभक्षताम् अश्नुते | पुत्री पशुमान् भवति सर्वम् आयुर् एति ||
text: Then follows (the teaching of) Kauntharavya.- There are three hundred and sixty letters, three himdred and sixty sibilants, three hundred and sixty unions. What we have called letters, they are the days. What we have called sibilants, they are the nights. What we have called unions, they are the unions of days and nights. So far as regards the deities. Now as regards the self. What we have called letters as regards the deities, these are bones as regards the self. What we have called sibilants as regards the deities, these are marrow as regards the self. This indeed is the chief breath, marrow. This is seed. Without breath, indeed, seed cannot be won. If without breath seed were effvised, it would decay, it would not be productive. What we have called unions as regards the deities, these are joints as regards the self. Of this triad, bones, marrow, joints, on this side there are five hundred and forty unions, on that side the same; this makes a thousand and eighty. One thousand and eighty BrhatI verses the singers' produce on this day as the (hymn of the) day. This is the self, commensurate with the day, composed of the eye, the ear, the metres, the mind, speech. He who knows thus this self, commensurate with the day, composed of the eye, the ear, the metres, the mind, speech, wins union and communion with the days, residence in the same world, and similarity of form. He becomes rich in cows and cattle. He lives all his days.
text_mt: Now Kauṣṭharavya [says]: "Three hundred and sixty syllables; three hundred and sixty sibilants; three hundred and sixty junctions. The syllables that we spoke of are days. The sibilants are nights. The junctions that we spoke of are the junctions of the days and nights." Thus with respect to the deities. Now with respect to the self: The syllables that we spoke of with respect to the deities are bones with respect to the self. The sibilants that we spoke of with respect to the deities are marrow with respect to the self. This marrow is indeed the immediate breath; it is semen. For without breath there is no accomplishment of semen. If semen were emitted without breath, it would rot and not develop. The junctions that we spoke of with respect to the deities are joints with respect to the self. Of this [person], of bones, marrow, and joints, there are five hundred and forty here; of junctions, there are five hundred and forty here—that makes eighty thousand. The followers of Arkali complete eighty thousand Bṛhatīs day by day. This same self is the measure of a day, consisting of sight, consisting of hearing, consisting of metre, consisting of mind, consisting of speech. He who thus knows this self, which is the measure of a day, consisting of sight, consisting of hearing, consisting of metre, consisting of mind, consisting of speech, attains union with the days, dwelling in the same world, having the same form, and sharing the same food. He becomes possessed of sons, possessed of cattle; he reaches a full lifespan.

sanskrit_iast: catvāraḥ puruṣā iti vāstyaḥ śarīrapuruṣaś chandaḥpuruṣo vedepuruṣo mahāpuruṣa iti | śarīrapuruṣa iti yam avocam ya evāyaṃ daivika ātmā tasyaitasya yo 'yam aśarīraḥ prajñātmā sa rasaḥ | chandaḥpuruṣa iti yam avocāmākṣarasamāmnāya eva | tasyaitasyākāro rasaḥ | vedapuruṣa iti yam avocāma yena devān vedargvedaṃ yajurvedaṃ sāmavedam iti tasyaitasya brahmarasaḥ | tasmād brahmiṣṭhaṃ brahmāṇam ṛtvijaṃ kurvīta yo yajñasyolvaṇaṃ vidyāt | mahāpuruṣa iti yam avocāma saṃvatsara eva tasyaitasyāsāv ādityo rasaḥ | sa yaś cāyam aśarīraḥ prajñātmā yaś cāsāv āditya ekam etad iti vidyāt | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
meaning: चत्वारः पुरुषा इति वास्त्यः शरीरपुरुषश् छन्दःपुरुषो वेदेपुरुषो महापुरुष इति | शरीरपुरुष इति यम् अवोचम् य एवायं दैविक आत्मा तस्यैतस्य यो ऽयम् अशरीरः प्रज्ञात्मा स रसः | छन्दःपुरुष इति यम् अवोचामाक्षरसमाम्नाय एव | तस्यैतस्याकारो रसः | वेदपुरुष इति यम् अवोचाम येन देवान् वेदर्ग्वेदं यजुर्वेदं सामवेदम् इति तस्यैतस्य ब्रह्मरसः | तस्माद् ब्रह्मिष्ठं ब्रह्माणम् ऋत्विजं कुर्वीत यो यज्ञस्योल्वणं विद्यात् | महापुरुष इति यम् अवोचाम संवत्सर एव तस्यैतस्यासाव् आदित्यो रसः | स यश् चायम् अशरीरः प्रज्ञात्मा यश् चासाव् आदित्य एकम् एतद् इति विद्यात् | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् ||
text: There are four persons,' says Vatsya, 'the person of the body, th person of the metres, the person of the Vedas, the great person.' What we have called the person of the body is the corporeal self. Of it the essence is this incorporeal intelligent self. What we have called the person of the metres is the alphabet. Of it the letter a is the essence. What we have called the person of the Vedas is that by which one knows the Vedas, the Rgveda, the Yajurveda, the Stimaveda. Of it the Brahman(n.) is the essence. Therefore one should take as priest a Brahman priest fullest of Brahman, who can know the unusuaP in the sacrifice. What we have called the great person is the year. Of it yonder sun is the essence. The incorporeal intelligent self here and yonder sun are the same, so one should know. This is declared in a Re.— ''
text_mt: "There are four persons," [says] Vātsya: "the bodily person, the person of metre, the person of the Veda, and the great person. As for the one we called the bodily person, this divine self—the bodiless conscious self is its essence. As for the one we called the person of metre, it is the enumeration of letters—the sound 'a' is its essence. As for the one we called the person of the Veda, by which one knows the gods—the Ṛgveda, the Yajurveda, the Sāmaveda—Brahman is its essence. Therefore one should appoint as the Brahman priest the one most versed in Brahman, who would know any excess in the sacrifice. As for the one we called the great person, it is the year—yonder sun is its essence." And he should know: "That which is this bodiless conscious self and that which is yonder sun—this is one." This has been declared by a verse:

sanskrit_iast: citraṃ devānām udagād anīkaṃ cakṣur mitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ | āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatas tasthuṣaś ca || iti | etām evānuvidyāṃ saṃhitāṃ saṃdhīyamānāṃ manya iti ha smāha vātsyaḥ etam u haiva bahvṛcā mahadukthe mīmāṃsanta etam agnāv adhvaryava etaṃ mahāvrate chandogā etam asyām etam antarikṣa etaṃ divi etam agnāv etaṃ vāyāv etaṃ candramasy etaṃ nakṣatreṣv etam apsv etam oṣadhīṣv etaṃ sarveṣu bhūteṣv etam akṣareṣv etam eva brahmetyupāsate | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
meaning: चित्रं देवानाम् उदगाद् अनीकं चक्षुर् मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः | आप्रा द्यावापृथिवी अन्तरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस् तस्थुषश् च || इति | एताम् एवानुविद्यां संहितां संधीयमानां मन्य इति ह स्माह वात्स्यः एतम् उ हैव बह्वृचा महदुक्थे मीमांसन्त एतम् अग्नाव् अध्वर्यव एतं महाव्रते छन्दोगा एतम् अस्याम् एतम् अन्तरिक्ष एतं दिवि एतम् अग्नाव् एतं वायाव् एतं चन्द्रमस्य् एतं नक्षत्रेष्व् एतम् अप्स्व् एतम् ओषधीष्व् एतं सर्वेषु भूतेष्व् एतम् अक्षरेष्व् एतम् एव ब्रह्मेत्युपासते | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् ||
text: The brilliant presence of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuna, and Agni. The soul of all that moveth not or moveth, the sun hath filled the air and earth and heaven.' 'Thus do I deem the union duly made,' says Vatsya. Him the Bahvrcas seek in the Mahad Uktha, him the Adhvaryus in the fire, him the Chandogas in the Mahavrata, him on earth, him in the atmosphere, him in the heaven, him in the fire, him in the wind, him in the moon, him in the Naksatras, SANKHAYANA AEANYAKA. 53 him in the waters, him in the plants, him in all beings, him in the letters, him they worship as Brahman. This is declared in a Re— 2
text_mt: "The wondrous face of the gods has arisen, / the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni; / it has filled heaven and earth and the intermediate space, / Sūrya, the self of the moving and the standing." / "It is according to this continuous text being joined together that I hold [this view]," Vātsya used to say. "It is him whom the Ṛgvedins investigate in the Great Recitation (mahaduktha); him the Adhvaryus in the fire altar; him the Sāmavedins in the Mahāvrata rite; him in this [earth], him in the intermediate space, him in heaven, him in fire, him in wind, him in the moon, him in the constellations, him in the waters, him in plants, him in all beings, him in syllables—it is him they revere as Brahman." This has been declared by a verse:

sanskrit_iast: ud vayaṃ tamasas pari jyotiṣ paśyanta uttaram | devaṃ devatrā sūryam aganma jyotir uttamam || iti | sa eṣo 'kṣarasaṃmānaś cakṣurmayaḥ śrotramayaś chandamayo manomayo vāṅmaya ātmā | sa ya evam etam akṣarasaṃānaṃ cakṣurmayaṃ śrotramayaṃ chandamayaṃ manomayaṃ vāṅmayam ātmānaṃ parasmai śaṃsati dugdhadohā asya vedā bhavanti | abhāgo vāci bhavati abhāgo 'nūkte | tad etad ṛcābhyuditam ||
meaning: उद् वयं तमसस् परि ज्योतिष् पश्यन्त उत्तरम् | देवं देवत्रा सूर्यम् अगन्म ज्योतिर् उत्तमम् || इति | स एषो ऽक्षरसंमानश् चक्षुर्मयः श्रोत्रमयश् छन्दमयो मनोमयो वाङ्मय आत्मा | स य एवम् एतम् अक्षरसंआनं चक्षुर्मयं श्रोत्रमयं छन्दमयं मनोमयं वाङ्मयम् आत्मानं परस्मै शंसति दुग्धदोहा अस्य वेदा भवन्ति | अभागो वाचि भवति अभागो ऽनूक्ते | तद् एतद् ऋचाभ्युदितम् ||
text: Looking upon the loftier light above the darkness we have come To Siirya, god among the gods, the light that is most excellent.' This is the self, commensurate with the letters, composed of the eye, the ear, the metres, the mind, speech. He who thus this self, commensurate with the letters, composed of the eye, the ear, the metres, the mind, speech, recites to another, his Vedas lose their savour, he has no part in speech, no part in what is studied. This is declared in a Re.— *
text_mt: "Seeing the higher light beyond darkness, / we have reached the god among the gods, / Sūrya, the highest light." / This same self is the measure of syllables, consisting of sight, consisting of hearing, consisting of metre, consisting of mind, consisting of speech. He who thus recites this self, which is the measure of syllables, consisting of sight, consisting of hearing, consisting of metre, consisting of mind, consisting of speech, to another—his Vedas become like milked-out cows. He has no share in speech; he has no share in what is recited. This has been declared by a verse:

sanskrit_iast: yas tityāja sacividaṃ sakhāyaṃ na tasya vācy api bhāgo asti | yad īṃ śṛnoty alakaṃ śṛṇoti na hi praveda sukṛtasya panthām || iti | nāsyānūkte vāco bhāgo astīty eva tad āha tan na parasmā etad ahaḥ śaṃset | nāgniṃ cinuyān na mahāvratena stuyān ned ātmano 'pihīyā iti | sa yaś cāyam aśarīraḥ prajñātmā yaś cāsāv āditya ekam etad ity avocāma tau yatra vipradṛśyete ||
meaning: यस् तित्याज सचिविदं सखायं न तस्य वाच्य् अपि भागो अस्ति | यद् ईं शृनोत्य् अलकं शृणोति न हि प्रवेद सुकृतस्य पन्थाम् || इति | नास्यानूक्ते वाचो भागो अस्तीत्य् एव तद् आह तन् न परस्मा एतद् अहः शंसेत् | नाग्निं चिनुयान् न महाव्रतेन स्तुयान् नेद् आत्मनो ऽपिहीया इति | स यश् चायम् अशरीरः प्रज्ञात्मा यश् चासाव् आदित्य एकम् एतद् इत्य् अवोचाम तौ यत्र विप्रदृश्येते ||
text: No part in speech hath he who hath abandoned his own dear friend who knows the truth of friendship. Even if he hears him, still in vain he listens; naught knows he of the path of righteous action.' In his study there is no part of speech, so he says. Therefore one should not recite (the litany of) that day for another, nor pile up the fire, nor celebrate the Mahavrata, lest he be torn away from his self. 'This incorporeal self here and yonder sun are one,' we have said. When these two are seen apart,
text_mt: "He who has abandoned a friend who shares knowledge / has no share even in speech. / Whatever he hears, he hears in vain; / for he does not know the path of virtuous action." / That is what it means when it says: "He has no share in speech, nor in what is recited." Therefore, one should not recite this day's [text] to another. One should not pile the fire altar, nor praise with the Mahāvrata rite, lest one be deprived of one's self. And that which we said: "That which is this bodiless conscious self and that which is yonder sun—this is one"—where they appear distinct...

sanskrit_iast: candramā ivādityo dṛśyate na raśmayaḥ prādur bhavanti | lohinī dyaur bhavati yathā mañjiṣṭhāḥ | vyastaḥ pāyur bhavati | saṃpareto 'syātmā na ciram iva jīviṣyatīti vidyāt | sa yat karaṇīyaṃ manyeta tat kuryāt | athāpyādarśe vodake vā jihmaśirasaṃ vāśirasaṃ vātmānaṃ paśyen na vā paśyet | tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi cchidrā chāyā bhavati na vā bhavati tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi cchidra ivādityo rathanābhir ivākhyāyet tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi nīla ivāgnir dṛśyeta yathā mayūragrīvā mahāmeghe vā marīcīr iva paśyet | anabhre vā vidyutaṃ paśyet | abhra enāṃ mna paśyet tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpy apidhāyākṣiṇī upekṣeta tatraitad varāṭakānīva na paśyet tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpy apidhāya karṇā upāsīta | ya eṣo 'gner iva jvalataḥ śabdo rathasyevopabdis taṃ na yadā śṛṇuyāt tad apy evam eva vidyāt | athāpi viparyaste kanyake dṛśyete dvijihmevā na vā dṛśyetetad apy evam eva vidyāt | sa yo 'to 'śruto 'mato 'vijñāto 'dṛṣṭo 'nādiṣṭo 'ghuṣṭaḥ śrotā mantā vijñātā draṣṭādeṣṭā ghoṣṭā sarveṣāṃ bhūtānām āntaraḥ puruṣaḥ sa ma ātmeti vidyāt | sa utkrāmann evaitam aśarīraṃ prajñātmānam abhisaṃpadyate vijahātītaraṃ dauhikam | saiṣā sarvasyai vāca upaniṣat | sarvā haivemāḥ sarvasyai vācaupaniṣadaḥ | imāṃ tv evam ācakṣate ||
meaning: चन्द्रमा इवादित्यो दृश्यते न रश्मयः प्रादुर् भवन्ति | लोहिनी द्यौर् भवति यथा मञ्जिष्ठाः | व्यस्तः पायुर् भवति | संपरेतो ऽस्यात्मा न चिरम् इव जीविष्यतीति विद्यात् | स यत् करणीयं मन्येत तत् कुर्यात् | अथाप्यादर्शे वोदके वा जिह्मशिरसं वाशिरसं वात्मानं पश्येन् न वा पश्येत् | तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथापि च्छिद्रा छाया भवति न वा भवति तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथापि च्छिद्र इवादित्यो रथनाभिर् इवाख्यायेत् तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथापि नील इवाग्निर् दृश्येत यथा मयूरग्रीवा महामेघे वा मरीचीर् इव पश्येत् | अनभ्रे वा विद्युतं पश्येत् | अभ्र एनां म्न पश्येत् तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथाप्य् अपिधायाक्षिणी उपेक्षेत तत्रैतद् वराटकानीव न पश्येत् तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथाप्य् अपिधाय कर्णा उपासीत | य एषो ऽग्नेर् इव ज्वलतः शब्दो रथस्येवोपब्दिस् तं न यदा शृणुयात् तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथापि विपर्यस्ते कन्यके दृश्येते द्विजिह्मेवा न वा दृश्येतेतद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | स यो ऽतो ऽश्रुतो ऽमतो ऽविज्ञातो ऽदृष्टो ऽनादिष्टो ऽघुष्टः श्रोता मन्ता विज्ञाता द्रष्टादेष्टा घोष्टा सर्वेषां भूतानाम् आन्तरः पुरुषः स म आत्मेति विद्यात् | स उत्क्रामन्न् एवैतम् अशरीरं प्रज्ञात्मानम् अभिसंपद्यते विजहातीतरं दौहिकम् | सैषा सर्वस्यै वाच उपनिषत् | सर्वा हैवेमाः सर्वस्यै वाचौपनिषदः | इमां त्व् एवम् आचक्षते ||
text: The sun appears like the moon, its rays do not shine forth, the sky is leaden like madder, the anus is gaping, 'the self in on the point of death, it will not live long,' so one should know. Whatever he considers should be done, he should do. Again, if he sees himself in a mirror or water with a crooked head or without a head, or cannot see himself, he should know that it is so. Again, if his shadow is pierced, or he throws no shadow, he should know that it is so. Again, if the sun appears pierced like the nave of a chariot wheel, he should know that it is so. Again, if the fire appears black like the neck of a peacock, or if amid a large cloud he should see as it were brightness, or when there is no cloud see lightning, or in cloudy weather see it not, he should know that it is so. Again, if closing his eyes he does not see motes, as it were, he should know that it is so. Again, if he shut his ears and listen, and does not then hear a noise as of burning fire or the sound of a chariot, he should know that it is so. Again, if the pupils of the eyes appear inverted or doubly crooked, or cannot be seen, he should know that it is so. 'The unheard, unthought, unknown, unseen, undirected, soundless hearer, thinker, knower, seer, director, sounder, the inner self of all beings, he is my soul,' so should one know. He departing enters into this incorporeal intelligent self, and abandons the other corporeal self. This is the Upaniṣad of speech as a whole. All these, indeed, are Upaniṣads of speech as a whole, but this one they call so especially.
text_mt: The sun is seen like the moon; rays do not appear. The sky becomes red like madder. The anus becomes prolapsed. One should know: 'His self has departed; he will not live much longer.' Whatever he thinks ought to be done, he should do it. Furthermore, if he should see himself in a mirror or in water with his head crooked or headless, or if he should not see [it at all], he should know it in just this way. Furthermore, when his shadow is perforated, or when it is not [cast at all], he should know it in just this way. Furthermore, if the sun should appear perforated, like the hub of a chariot-wheel, he should know it in just this way. Furthermore, if fire should appear blue like the neck of a peacock, or if he should see mirages in a great cloud, or if he should see lightning when the sky is cloudless, or if he should not see it in a cloud, he should know it in just this way. Furthermore, having closed his eyes, if he should look closely and not see there those [spots] like cowrie-shells, he should know it in just this way. Furthermore, having covered his ears, if he should sit and not hear that sound like blazing fire or the rumbling of a chariot, he should know it in just this way. Furthermore, if his pupils are seen inverted, or as if double-tongued, or are not seen at all, he should know it in just this way. The one who is unheard, unthought, unknown, unseen, unindicated, unproclaimed, the hearer, thinker, knower, seer, indicator, proclaimer, the inner person of all beings—he should know: 'He is my self.' Rising up [at death], he attains this bodiless conscious self; he leaves behind the other, which belongs to the body. This is the secret teaching (upaniṣad) of all speech. For indeed, all these are secret teachings of all speech; but this one they declare in this way.

sanskrit_iast: pṛthivyā rūpaṃ sparśā antarikṣasyoṣmāṇo divaḥ svarāḥ | agne rūpaṃ sparśā vāyor ūṣmāṇa ādityasya svarāḥ | ṛgvedasya rūpaṃ sparśā yajurvedasyoṣmāṇaḥ sāmavedasya svarāḥ | rathantarasya rūpaṃ sparśā vāmadevyasyoṣmāṇo bṛhataḥ svarāḥ | prāṇasya rūpaṃ sparśā apānasyoṣmāṇo manasaḥ svarāḥ | prāṇasya rūpaṃ sparśā apānasyoṣmāṇa udānasya svarāḥ svarā iti punardattaḥ | eṣa u haiva sarvāṃ vācaṃ veda ya evaṃ veda ||
meaning: पृथिव्या रूपं स्पर्शा अन्तरिक्षस्योष्माणो दिवः स्वराः | अग्ने रूपं स्पर्शा वायोर् ऊष्माण आदित्यस्य स्वराः | ऋग्वेदस्य रूपं स्पर्शा यजुर्वेदस्योष्माणः सामवेदस्य स्वराः | रथन्तरस्य रूपं स्पर्शा वामदेव्यस्योष्माणो बृहतः स्वराः | प्राणस्य रूपं स्पर्शा अपानस्योष्माणो मनसः स्वराः | प्राणस्य रूपं स्पर्शा अपानस्योष्माण उदानस्य स्वराः स्वरा इति पुनर्दत्तः | एष उ हैव सर्वां वाचं वेद य एवं वेद ||
text: The mutes are the form of earth, the sibilants of the atmosphere, the vowels of the heaven. The mutes are the form of Agni, the sibilants of Vayu, and the vowels of Aditya. The mutes are the form of the Rgveda, the sibilants of the Yajurveda, the vowels of the Samaveda. The mutes are the form of the Rathantara, the sibilants of the Vamadevya, the vowels of the Brhat. The mutes are the form of expiration, the sibilants of inspiration, the vowels of Vyana.- The mutes are the form of expiration, the sibilants of inspiration, the vowels of mind. 'The mutes are the form of expiration, the sibilants of inspiration, the vowels of Udana,' says SANKHAYANA AEANYAKA. 55 Punardatta. He, indeed, knows speech as a whole who knows this.
text_mt: The stop-consonants are the form of earth, the sibilants of the intermediate space, the vowels of heaven. The stop-consonants are the form of Agni, the sibilants of Vāyu, the vowels of the Sun. The stop-consonants are the form of the Ṛgveda, the sibilants of the Yajurveda, the vowels of the Sāmaveda. The stop-consonants are the form of the Rathantara [sāman], the sibilants of the Vāmadevya, the vowels of the Bṛhat. The stop-consonants are the form of the in-breath, the sibilants of the out-breath, the vowels of the mind. The stop-consonants are the form of the in-breath, the sibilants of the out-breath, the vowels of the up-breath: 'the vowels,' thus [taught] Punardatta. He indeed knows all speech who knows thus.

sanskrit_iast: atha khalv iyaṃ daivī vīṇā bhavati tadanukṛtir asau mānuṣī bhavati | tad yatheyaṃ śastravatī tardmavatī bhavaty evam evāsau śastravatī tardmavatī bhavati | tad yathāsyāḥ śira evam amuṣyāḥ śiraḥ | tad yathāsyai vaṃśa evam amuṣyā daṇḍaḥ | tad yathāsyā udaram evam amuṣyā ambhaṇaṃ | tad yathāsyai mukhanāsike akṣiṇī ity evam amuṣyāś chidrāṇi | tad yathāsyā aṅgulinigrahā upastaraṇānīty evam amuṣyāḥ parvāṇi | tad yathāsyā aṅgulaya evam amuṣyās tantryaḥ | tad yathāsyai jihvaivam amuṣyā vādanam | tad yathāsyāḥ svarā evam amuṣyāḥ svarāḥ | tad yathā haiveyaṃ romaśena carmaṇāpihitā bhavaty evam evāsau romaśena carmaṇāpihitā bhavati | romaśena ha sma carmaṇā purā vīṇā apidadhati | saiṣā daivī vīṇā bhavati | sa ya evam etāṃ daivīṃ vīṇāṃ veda śrutavadanatamo bhavati bhūmiprāsya kīrtir bhavati śuśrūṣante hāsya parṣatsu bhāṣyamāṇasyedam astu yad ayam īhate yatrāryā vāg vadati vidur enaṃ tatra ||
meaning: अथ खल्व् इयं दैवी वीणा भवति तदनुकृतिर् असौ मानुषी भवति | तद् यथेयं शस्त्रवती तर्द्मवती भवत्य् एवम् एवासौ शस्त्रवती तर्द्मवती भवति | तद् यथास्याः शिर एवम् अमुष्याः शिरः | तद् यथास्यै वंश एवम् अमुष्या दण्डः | तद् यथास्या उदरम् एवम् अमुष्या अम्भणं | तद् यथास्यै मुखनासिके अक्षिणी इत्य् एवम् अमुष्याश् छिद्राणि | तद् यथास्या अङ्गुलिनिग्रहा उपस्तरणानीत्य् एवम् अमुष्याः पर्वाणि | तद् यथास्या अङ्गुलय एवम् अमुष्यास् तन्त्र्यः | तद् यथास्यै जिह्वैवम् अमुष्या वादनम् | तद् यथास्याः स्वरा एवम् अमुष्याः स्वराः | तद् यथा हैवेयं रोमशेन चर्मणापिहिता भवत्य् एवम् एवासौ रोमशेन चर्मणापिहिता भवति | रोमशेन ह स्म चर्मणा पुरा वीणा अपिदधति | सैषा दैवी वीणा भवति | स य एवम् एतां दैवीं वीणां वेद श्रुतवदनतमो भवति भूमिप्रास्य कीर्तिर् भवति शुश्रूषन्ते हास्य पर्षत्सु भाष्यमाणस्येदम् अस्तु यद् अयम् ईहते यत्रार्या वाग् वदति विदुर् एनं तत्र ||
text: Again, there is this divine lute. That human lute is an imitation of it. As this has a sounding-board and is tightly strung, so has that a sounding-board and is tightly strung. As this has a head, so that has a head. As this has a spine, so that has a bridge. As this has a belly, so that has a cavitj As this has mouth, nose, and eyes, so that has holes. As this has joints, so that has finger-catches and covers. As this has fingers, so that has strings. As this has a tongue, so that has a sounder. As this has sounds, so that has sounds. As this is covered with a hairy skin, so that is covered with a hairy skin. For with a hairy skin they used of old to cover lutes. This is the divine lute. He who knows thus this divine lute becomes exceedingly famous; his renown fills the earth; men hearken to him when he speaks in the assemblies, (saying), 'Let this be done which he desires.' "Where Aryan speech is uttered they know him there.
text_mt: Now indeed, this is the divine lute; that human one is an imitation of it. Just as this [body] has a head and has cavities, so also that [lute] has a head and has cavities. Just as this has a head, so that has a head. Just as this has a spine, so that has a neck. Just as this has a belly, so that has a sounding-board. Just as this has a mouth, nostrils, and eyes, so that has apertures. Just as this has finger-joints and coverings, so that has frets. Just as this has fingers, so that has strings. Just as this has a tongue, so that has a plectrum. Just as this has vowels, so that has notes. And just as this is covered with hairy skin, so also that is covered with hairy skin. Formerly, indeed, they used to cover lutes with hairy skin. This is that divine lute. He who knows this divine lute thus becomes most famous as a speaker; his fame fills the earth; and they desire to listen to him when he speaks in assemblies: 'Let whatever this man desires come to be!' Wherever noble speech is spoken, there they know him.

sanskrit_iast: athātas tāṇḍavindasya vacaḥ | tad yatheyaṃ akuśalena vādayitrāvīṇārabdhā na kṛtsnaṃ vīṇārthaṃ sādhayaty evam evākuśalena vaktrā vāg ārabdhā na kṛtsnaṃ vāg arthaṃ sādhayati | tad yathā haiveyaṃ kuśalena vādayitrā vīṇārabdhā kṛtsnaṃ vīṇārthaṃ sādhayaty evam eva kuśalena vaktrā vāg ārabdhā kṛtsnaṃ vāg arthaṃ sādhayati | tasyai vā etasyai vīṇāyai yā tviṣiḥ sā saṃhiteti kātyāyanīputro jātūkarṇyaḥ | atha ha smaitat kṛtsnahārito brāhmaṇam evodāharati ||
meaning: अथातस् ताण्डविन्दस्य वचः | तद् यथेयं अकुशलेन वादयित्रावीणारब्धा न कृत्स्नं वीणार्थं साधयत्य् एवम् एवाकुशलेन वक्त्रा वाग् आरब्धा न कृत्स्नं वाग् अर्थं साधयति | तद् यथा हैवेयं कुशलेन वादयित्रा वीणारब्धा कृत्स्नं वीणार्थं साधयत्य् एवम् एव कुशलेन वक्त्रा वाग् आरब्धा कृत्स्नं वाग् अर्थं साधयति | तस्यै वा एतस्यै वीणायै या त्विषिः सा संहितेति कात्यायनीपुत्रो जातूकर्ण्यः | अथ ह स्मैतत् कृत्स्नहारितो ब्राह्मणम् एवोदाहरति ||
text: Then follows the saying of Tiindavindava. As a lute struck by an unskilled player fulfils not the full purpose of a lute, so speech set in motion by an unskilled speaker fulfils not the full purpose of speech. As a lute struck by a skilled player fulfils the full purpose of a lute, so speech set in motion by a skilled speaker fulfils the full purpose of speech. 'Of this lute the splendour is the union,' says the son of KatyayanI, Jiitukarnya. Now Krtsna Harita sets forth a Brahmana.'
text_mt: Now then, the saying of Tāṇḍavinda. Just as this lute, taken up by an unskilful player, does not achieve the complete purpose of the lute, so speech, taken up by an unskilful speaker, does not achieve the complete purpose of speech. And just as this lute, taken up by a skilful player, achieves the complete purpose of the lute, so speech, taken up by a skilful speaker, achieves the complete purpose of speech. 'The splendour of this very lute is the continuous text (saṃhitā),' says Jātūkarṇya, the son of Kātyāyanī. And Kṛtsnahārita indeed cited a Brāhmaṇa passage concerning this:

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatiḥ prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā vyasraṃsata sa chandobhir ātmānaṃ samadadhat | tad yac chandobhir ātmānaṃ samadadhat tasmāt saṃhitā | tasyai vā etasyai saṃhitāyai ṇakaro balaṃ ṣakāraḥ prāṇa ātmā saṃhitā | athaiṣā kṣudramiśrā vikṛtis tāni nakhāni romāṇi vyañjanānīti | sa yo 'tra vicikitset saṇakāraṃ eva brūyād ṛte ṇakāram iti saṇakāram eva brūyāt | evam eva yo 'tra vicikitset saṣakāraṃ eva brūyād ṛte ṣakāram iti saṣakāram eva brūyāt | tau vā etau ṇakāraṣakārau vidvān anusaṃhitam ṛco 'dhīyītāyuṣyam iti vidyād evam eva vidyāt | atha vāg itihāsapurāṇaṃ yac cānyat kiṃcid brāhmīkṛtyevādhīyīta tad apy evam eva vidyāt | te yad vayam anusaṃhitam ṛco 'dhīmahe yac ca māṇḍūkeyīyam adhyāyaṃ prabrūmas tena no ṇakāraṣakārā upāptāv iti ha smāha hrasvo māṇḍūkeyaḥ | atha yad vayam anusaṃhitam ṛco 'dhīmahe yac ca svādhyāyam adhīmahe tena no ṇakāraṣakārā upāptāv iti ha smāha sthaviraḥ śākalyaḥ | etad dha sma vai tad vidvāṃsa āhuḥ kāvaṣeyāḥ kimarthā vayaṃ yakṣyāmahe kimarthā vayam adheṣyāmahe vāci hi prāṇaṃ juhumaḥ prāṇe vācaṃ yo hy eva prabhavaḥ sa evāpyaya iti | tā etāḥ saṃhitā nānantevāsine brūyān nāsaṃvatsaravāsine nābrahmacāriṇe nāvedavide nāpavaktra ity ācāryā ity ācāryāḥ ||
meaning: प्रजापतिः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा व्यस्रंसत स छन्दोभिर् आत्मानं समदधत् | तद् यच् छन्दोभिर् आत्मानं समदधत् तस्मात् संहिता | तस्यै वा एतस्यै संहितायै णकरो बलं षकारः प्राण आत्मा संहिता | अथैषा क्षुद्रमिश्रा विकृतिस् तानि नखानि रोमाणि व्यञ्जनानीति | स यो ऽत्र विचिकित्सेत् सणकारं एव ब्रूयाद् ऋते णकारम् इति सणकारम् एव ब्रूयात् | एवम् एव यो ऽत्र विचिकित्सेत् सषकारं एव ब्रूयाद् ऋते षकारम् इति सषकारम् एव ब्रूयात् | तौ वा एतौ णकारषकारौ विद्वान् अनुसंहितम् ऋचो ऽधीयीतायुष्यम् इति विद्याद् एवम् एव विद्यात् | अथ वाग् इतिहासपुराणं यच् चान्यत् किंचिद् ब्राह्मीकृत्येवाधीयीत तद् अप्य् एवम् एव विद्यात् | ते यद् वयम् अनुसंहितम् ऋचो ऽधीमहे यच् च माण्डूकेयीयम् अध्यायं प्रब्रूमस् तेन नो णकारषकारा उपाप्ताव् इति ह स्माह ह्रस्वो माण्डूकेयः | अथ यद् वयम् अनुसंहितम् ऋचो ऽधीमहे यच् च स्वाध्यायम् अधीमहे तेन नो णकारषकारा उपाप्ताव् इति ह स्माह स्थविरः शाकल्यः | एतद् ध स्म वै तद् विद्वांस आहुः कावषेयाः किमर्था वयं यक्ष्यामहे किमर्था वयम् अधेष्यामहे वाचि हि प्राणं जुहुमः प्राणे वाचं यो ह्य् एव प्रभवः स एवाप्यय इति | ता एताः संहिता नानन्तेवासिने ब्रूयान् नासंवत्सरवासिने नाब्रह्मचारिणे नावेदविदे नापवक्त्र इत्य् आचार्या इत्य् आचार्याः ||
text: Prajāpati having created creatures fell to pieces. He united himself by means of the metres. Because he united himself by means of the metres, there is the union. Of this union the letter na is strength, the letter sa breath, the self the union. 66 SA.NKHAYANA ARANYAKA. As for this modification (in which gross are) combined with minute (elements), they are nails, hairs, consonants. If he should be in doubt whether to say it with a na or without a na, let him say it with a iia. So if he should be in doubt whether to say it with a m or without a sa, let him say it with the sa. Knowing these two letters 7ia and sa one should study the Re verses according to the Samhitii text. Let him know that it is lifegiving. Again, speech is the Itihasapurana, and whatever else there is of holy work; this should one study; let him know this also (to be lifegiving). 'In that we study the Re verses according to the Samhita and speak forth the recitation of Mandukeya, so we secure the letters na and sa,' says Hrasva Mandukeya. Again, In that we study the Re verses according to the Sarnhita and learn the recitation, so we secure the letters na and m,' says Sthavira Sakalya. Knowing that the Kavaseyas say, For what purpose shall we sacrifice, for what purpose shall we study? For in speech we offer breath, in breath speech. The source is also the scene of disappearance.' 'These Saṃhitās one should not proclaim to one who is not a pupil, who is not a pupil for a year, who is not a student, who is not a knower of the Vedas, who is not to be a teacher,' so say the teachers.
text_mt: Prajāpati, having created creatures, fell apart. He put himself together with the metres. Because he put himself together with the metres, therefore [it is called] continuous text (saṃhitā). Of this very continuous text, the sound ṇa is strength, the sound ṣa is breath, and the self is the continuous text. Now, this modification mixed with small parts consists of nails, hairs, and consonants. If anyone should hesitate here, [wondering,] 'Should one pronounce it with the sound ṇa or without the sound ṇa?', he should pronounce it only with the sound ṇa. In the same way, if anyone should hesitate here, [wondering,] 'Should one pronounce it with the sound ṣa or without the sound ṣa?', he should pronounce it only with the sound ṣa. Knowing these two sounds, ṇa and ṣa, he should recite the verses according to the continuous text (saṃhitā); he should know: 'It brings long life'—he should know it in just this way. Moreover, whatever speech, narrative, ancient lore, and whatever else [there is], he should study it having made it, as it were, sacred; he should know it in just this way. 'In that we recite the verses according to the continuous text, and in that we teach the lesson of Māṇḍūkeya, thereby we have obtained the sounds ṇa and ṣa,' said the short Māṇḍūkeya. 'Moreover, in that we recite the verses according to the continuous text, and in that we recite our daily study, thereby we have obtained the sounds ṇa and ṣa,' said the elder Śākalya. Indeed, knowing this, the descendants of Kavaṣa used to say: 'Why should we sacrifice? Why should we study? For we offer breath into speech, and speech into breath; for whatever is the origin, that alone is the dissolution.' One should not teach these continuous texts to one who is not a pupil, nor to one who has not resided for a year, nor to one who is not a chaste student (brahmacārin), nor to one who does not know the Veda, nor to a detractor—thus the teachers, thus the teachers.

sanskrit_iast: om | tat savitur vṛṇīmahe | vayaṃ devasya bhojanam | śreṣṭhaṃ sarvadhātamam | turaṃ bhagasya dhīmahi | tat savitur vareṇyaṃ | bhargo devasya dhīmahi | dhiyo yo naḥ pracodayāt || adabdhaṃ mana iṣiraṃ cakṣuḥ | sūryo jyotiṣāṃ śreṣṭho dīkṣe mā mā hiṃsīḥ ||
meaning: ओम् | तत् सवितुर् वृणीमहे | वयं देवस्य भोजनम् | श्रेष्ठं सर्वधातमम् | तुरं भगस्य धीमहि | तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यं | भर्गो देवस्य धीमहि | धियो यो नः प्रचोदयात् || अदब्धं मन इषिरं चक्षुः | सूर्यो ज्योतिषां श्रेष्ठो दीक्षे मा मा हिंसीः ||
text: Om. We crave of Savitr the god this treasure much to be enjoyed. The best, all-yielding, conquering gift of Bhaga gladly we would win. May we attain the excellent glory of Savitr the god: So may he stimulate our prayers. Mind undeceived, living eye, sun best of lights. Consecration harm me not.
text_mt: Om. / That food of the god Savitṛ we choose, / best, all-sustaining; / the swift bounty of Bhaga we meditate upon. / That excellent splendour of the god Savitṛ / we meditate upon, / who may inspire our thoughts. / Mind undeceived, eye active, / the sun, the best of lights: O consecration, do not harm me!

sanskrit_iast: yo ha vai jyeṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca veda jyeṣṭhaś ca ha vai śreṣṭhaś ca svānāṃ bhavati | prāṇo vai jyeṣṭhaś ca śreṣṭhaś ca | yo ha vai vasiṣṭhāṃ veda vasiṣṭho ha svānāṃ bhavati vāg vai vasiṣṭhā | yo ha vai pratiṣṭhāṃ veda prati ha tiṣṭhaty asmiṃś ca loke 'muṣmiṃś ca cakṣur ha pratiṣṭhā | yo ha vai saṃpadaṃ veda saṃ hāsmai kāmāḥ saṃpadyante śrotraṃ ha vā u saṃpat | yo ha vā āyatanaṃ vedāyatano ha svānāṃ bhavati mano vā āyatanam | atha hemā devatāḥ prajāpatiṃ pitaram etyābruvan ko vai naḥ śreṣṭha iti | sa hovāca prajāpatir yasmin va utkrānte śarīraṃ pāpiṣṭham iva manyate sa vai śreṣṭha iti ||
meaning: यो ह वै ज्येष्ठं च श्रेष्ठं च वेद ज्येष्ठश् च ह वै श्रेष्ठश् च स्वानां भवति | प्राणो वै ज्येष्ठश् च श्रेष्ठश् च | यो ह वै वसिष्ठां वेद वसिष्ठो ह स्वानां भवति वाग् वै वसिष्ठा | यो ह वै प्रतिष्ठां वेद प्रति ह तिष्ठत्य् अस्मिंश् च लोके ऽमुष्मिंश् च चक्षुर् ह प्रतिष्ठा | यो ह वै संपदं वेद सं हास्मै कामाः संपद्यन्ते श्रोत्रं ह वा उ संपत् | यो ह वा आयतनं वेदायतनो ह स्वानां भवति मनो वा आयतनम् | अथ हेमा देवताः प्रजापतिं पितरम् एत्याब्रुवन् को वै नः श्रेष्ठ इति | स होवाच प्रजापतिर् यस्मिन् व उत्क्रान्ते शरीरं पापिष्ठम् इव मन्यते स वै श्रेष्ठ इति ||
text: He who knows the highest and best becomes highest and best among his own (people). Breath indeed is the highest and best. He who knows the most excellent becomes the most excellent among his own (people). Speech indeed is the most excellent. He who knows the support finds support both in this world and in that. The eye indeed is support. He who knows obtainment, his desires are obtained together for him. The ear indeed is obtainment. He who knows the resort becomes the resort of his own (people). Mind indeed is the resort. These deities approached Prajapati and said, 'Who indeed is the best of us?' Prajapati said, 'He is the best on whose departure the body considers itself worst as it were.'
text_mt: : Whoever knows the eldest and best becomes the eldest and best among his own people. Breath indeed is the eldest and best. Whoever knows the richest becomes the richest among his own people; speech indeed is the richest. Whoever knows the foundation is established both in this world and in yonder world; sight indeed is the foundation. Whoever knows attainment, to him desires are attained; hearing indeed is attainment. Whoever knows the abode becomes an abode for his own people; the mind indeed is the abode. Then these deities went to Prajāpati, their father, and said: "Who of us is the best?" Prajāpati said: "He on whose departure the body is considered the most wretched, he is the best."

sanskrit_iast: sā ha vāg uccakrāma | yathā mūkā avadantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena paśyantaś cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ||
meaning: सा ह वाग् उच्चक्राम | यथा मूका अवदन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन पश्यन्तश् चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ||
text: Speech departed. They were like dumb men, speechless, breathing with breath, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind.
text_mt: : Speech departed. [The others remained] just like mutes not speaking, breathing with breath, seeing with sight, hearing with hearing, thinking with the mind—just so.

sanskrit_iast: cakṣur hoccakrāma | yathāndhā apaśyantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇa dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ||
meaning: चक्षुर् होच्चक्राम | यथान्धा अपश्यन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेण ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ||
text: Sight departed. They were like blind men, sightless, breathing with breath, speaking with speech, hearing with the ear, thinking with the mind.
text_mt: : Sight departed. [The others remained] just like the blind not seeing, breathing with breath, speaking with speech, hearing with hearing, thinking with the mind—just so.

sanskrit_iast: śrotraṃ hoccakrāma | yathā badhirā aśṛṇvantaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaḥ cakṣuṣā dhyāyanto manasaivam iti ||
meaning: श्रोत्रं होच्चक्राम | यथा बधिरा अशृण्वन्तः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तः चक्षुषा ध्यायन्तो मनसैवम् इति ||
text: Hearing departed. They were like deaf men, devoid of hearing, breathing with breath, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, thinking with the mind.
text_mt: : Hearing departed. [The others remained] just like the deaf not hearing, breathing with breath, speaking with speech, seeing with sight, thinking with the mind—just so.

sanskrit_iast: mano hoccakrāma | yathā bālā amanasaḥ prāṇantaḥ prāṇena vadanto vācā paśyantaḥ cakṣuṣā śṛṇvantaḥ śrotreṇaivam iti ||
meaning: मनो होच्चक्राम | यथा बाला अमनसः प्राणन्तः प्राणेन वदन्तो वाचा पश्यन्तः चक्षुषा शृण्वन्तः श्रोत्रेणैवम् इति ||
text: Mind departed. They were like infants, without mind, breathing with breath, speaking with speech, seeing with the eye, hearing with the ear.
text_mt: : The mind departed. [The others remained] just like children lacking mind, breathing with breath, speaking with speech, seeing with sight, hearing with hearing—just so.

sanskrit_iast: prāṇo hoccakrāma | tatas tad yatheha saindhavaḥ suhayaḥ paḍbīśaśaṅkūn saṃkhided evam asau prāṇān samakhidat | te ha sametyocur bhagavan motkramīr iti | sa hovāca prāṇaḥ kiṃ me 'nnaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | yat kiṃcāśvabhya ivāśakunibhya iti | kiṃ me vāso bhaviṣyatīty āpa iti hocuḥ | tasmād vā ayam aśiṣyan purastāc copariṣṭāc cādbhiḥ paridadhāti | lambhuko hāsya vāso bhavaty anagno hi bhavati | had dha smaitat satyakāmo jābālo gośrute vaiyāghrapadyāyoktvovāca | apy evaṃ śuṣkasya sthāṇoḥ prabrūyāj jayerann asya śākhāḥ praroheyuḥ palāśanīti | vanaspate śatavalśo viroheti dyāṃ mā lekhīr antarikṣaṃ mā mā hiṃsīr iti ha yājñavalkyaḥ ||
meaning: प्राणो होच्चक्राम | ततस् तद् यथेह सैन्धवः सुहयः पड्बीशशङ्कून् संखिदेद् एवम् असौ प्राणान् समखिदत् | ते ह समेत्योचुर् भगवन् मोत्क्रमीर् इति | स होवाच प्राणः किं मे ऽन्नं भविष्यतीति | यत् किंचाश्वभ्य इवाशकुनिभ्य इति | किं मे वासो भविष्यतीत्य् आप इति होचुः | तस्माद् वा अयम् अशिष्यन् पुरस्ताच् चोपरिष्टाच् चाद्भिः परिदधाति | लम्भुको हास्य वासो भवत्य् अनग्नो हि भवति | हद् ध स्मैतत् सत्यकामो जाबालो गोश्रुते वैयाघ्रपद्यायोक्त्वोवाच | अप्य् एवं शुष्कस्य स्थाणोः प्रब्रूयाज् जयेरन्न् अस्य शाखाः प्ररोहेयुः पलाशनीति | वनस्पते शतवल्शो विरोहेति द्यां मा लेखीर् अन्तरिक्षं मा मा हिंसीर् इति ह याज्ञवल्क्यः ||
text: Breath departed. Then just as a fine steed from the Indus strains the pin of his hobbles, so he strained the breaths. They assembled and said, 'Lord, depart not.' Breath said, What will be my food? ' 'All there is up to dogs, up to birds.' 'What will be my clothing? ' 'The waters,' they replied. Therefore a man about to eat purifies himself before and after with water. He is eager to take his clothing, for he is not naked. This Satyakama Jabala declared to Gosruta Vaiyiighrapadya and said, 'If one declared this to a dry stump, there would arise from it branches, there w ould spring up blossoms.' 'Spring forth, tree, with a hundred blossoms. Harm not the sky, harm not the atmosphere,' says Yajnavalkya.'
text_mt: : Breath departed. Then, just as in this world a noble Indus steed might tear out the tethering pegs of its hobbles, so did it tear out the [other] vital breaths. They assembled and said: "Venerable sir, do not depart!" Breath said: "What shall be my food?" "Whatever there is, even down to dogs and birds," they said. "What shall be my clothing?" "Water," they said. Therefore, when about to eat, one surrounds it with water both beforehand and afterwards. He becomes a receiver of clothing; indeed, he is not naked. Having spoken this to Gośruta Vaiyāghrapadya, Satyakāma Jābāla said: "Even if one were to tell this to a dry stump, its branches would be born and leaves would sprout forth: 'O tree, sprout with a hundred branches! Do not scratch heaven! Do not harm the intermediate space!' Thus said Yājñavalkya."

sanskrit_iast: atha yadi mahaj jigamiṣet trirātraṃ dīkṣitvāmāvāsyāyāṃ sarvauṣadasya manthaṃ dadhimadhubhyām upamanthyāgnim upassamādhāya parisamuhya paristīrya paryukṣya dakṣiṇaṃ jānv ācyottarato 'gneḥ kaṃse manthaṃ kṛtvā hutvā homān manthe saṃpātaṃ ānayet | jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāya svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃpātam ānayet | pratiṣṭhāyai svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃpātam ānayet | saṃpade svāhety agnau hutvā manthe saṃpātam ānayet | tat savitur vareṇyam iti pacchaḥ prāśya tat savitur vṛṇīmaha iti paccha ācāmati mahāvyāhṛtibhiś caturthaṃ nirṇijya kāṃsyaṃ carmaṇi vā sthaṇḍile vā saṃviśati | sa yadi striyaṃ paśyet samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt samṛddhaṃ karmeti vidyāt ||
meaning: अथ यदि महज् जिगमिषेत् त्रिरात्रं दीक्षित्वामावास्यायां सर्वौषदस्य मन्थं दधिमधुभ्याम् उपमन्थ्याग्निम् उपस्समाधाय परिसमुह्य परिस्तीर्य पर्युक्ष्य दक्षिणं जान्व् आच्योत्तरतो ऽग्नेः कंसे मन्थं कृत्वा हुत्वा होमान् मन्थे संपातं आनयेत् | ज्येष्ठाय श्रेष्ठाय स्वाहेत्य् अग्नौ हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् आनयेत् | प्रतिष्ठायै स्वाहेत्य् अग्नौ हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् आनयेत् | संपदे स्वाहेत्य् अग्नौ हुत्वा मन्थे संपातम् आनयेत् | तत् सवितुर् वरेण्यम् इति पच्छः प्राश्य तत् सवितुर् वृणीमह इति पच्छ आचामति महाव्याहृतिभिश् चतुर्थं निर्णिज्य कांस्यं चर्मणि वा स्थण्डिले वा संविशति | स यदि स्त्रियं पश्येत् समृद्धं कर्मेति विद्यात् समृद्धं कर्मेति विद्यात् ||
text: Now if one desires to obtain something important, after consecrating himself for three nights, on the night of new moon, having mixed wath curds and honey a mess of all sorts of herbs, having built up the fire, having swept (the place of sacrifice), having scattered (grass) about, having sprinkled water, bending the right knee, he places the mess in a vessel to the north of the fire, sacrifices, and pours into the mess the remainder of the oblation. 'Svdhd to the highest and best,' (with these words) having sacrificed in the fire, he should pour the rest into the mess. 'Svahd to the most excellent,' (with these words) having sacrificed in the fire, he should pour the rest into the mess. 'Svdlid to support,' (with these words) having sacrificed in the fire, he should pour the rest into the mess. 'Svd/id to obtainment,' (with these words) having sacrificed in the fire, he should pour the rest into the mess. 'Svdhd to resort,' (with these words) having sacrificed in the fire, he should pour the rest into the mess.' Having eaten, (repeating) by quarter-verses 'We crave of Savitr,' he sips, (repeating) by quarter-verses 'The excellent (glory) of Savitr,' the fourth (sij)) being accompanied by the Yyahrtis. Then he washes the vessel and goes to rest on a skin or on the bare ground. If he sees a w oman, he should know that his rite is successful.
text_mt: : Now, if one wishes to attain greatness, having consecrated oneself for three nights, on the new moon day, having mixed a mash of all herbs with curds and honey, having built up the fire, swept around it, strewn [grass] around it, and sprinkled it with water, having bent the right knee, having placed the mash in a bronze vessel north of the fire, having offered the oblations, one should drop the remainder into the mash. Having offered into the fire, saying, 'To the eldest, to the best, svāhā!', one should drop the remainder into the mash. Having offered into the fire, saying, 'To the foundation, svāhā!', one should drop the remainder into the mash. Having offered into the fire, saying, 'To attainment, svāhā!', one should drop the remainder into the mash. Having consumed [the mash] quarter-verse by quarter-verse with 'That excellent splendour of Savitṛ...', one sips water quarter-verse by quarter-verse with 'That food of the god Savitṛ we choose...'. Having rinsed the bronze vessel a fourth time with the great mystical utterances, one lies down on a skin or on the bare ground. If he should see a woman, he should know: 'The rite is successful! The rite is successful!'

sanskrit_iast: athāto 'dhyātmikam | āntaram agnihotram ity ācakṣate | etā ha vai devatāḥ puruṣa eva pratiṣṭhitā agnir vāci vāyuḥ prāṇa ādityaś cakṣuṣi candramā manasi diśaḥ śrotra āpo retasi | etāsu ha vai sarvāsu hutaṃ bhavati ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca | so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: अथातो ऽध्यात्मिकम् | आन्तरम् अग्निहोत्रम् इत्य् आचक्षते | एता ह वै देवताः पुरुष एव प्रतिष्ठिता अग्निर् वाचि वायुः प्राण आदित्यश् चक्षुषि चन्द्रमा मनसि दिशः श्रोत्र आपो रेतसि | एतासु ह वै सर्वासु हुतं भवति य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च | सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: Then follows the internal Agnihotra relating to the self. So they describe it. These deities, indeed, are established in man; fire in speech, wind in breath, sun in the eye, moon in the mind, the quarters in the ear, the waters in the seed. In all of these is offering made by him who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: : Now therefore [the rite] relating to the self. They call it the inner agnihotra. These deities are established in the person: Agni in speech, Vāyu in breath, Āditya in sight, the moon in the mind, the quarters of space in hearing, the waters in semen. An oblation is offered into all these when one who knows thus eats and drinks, and causes [others] to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies [others].

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛpto vācaṃ tarpayati | vāk tṛptāgniṃ tarpayati | agnis tṛptaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayati | pṛthivī tṛptā yat kiṃcit pṛthhivyāpihitaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: स तृप्तो वाचं तर्पयति | वाक् तृप्ताग्निं तर्पयति | अग्निस् तृप्तः पृथिवीं तर्पयति | पृथिवी तृप्ता यत् किंचित् पृथ्हिव्यापिहितं भवद् भविष्यद् भूतं तत् सर्वं तर्पयति | य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: He delighted delights speech, speech delighted delights fire, fire delighted delights earth, earth delighted whatever is covered by earth. Present, future, past, all that he delights, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: He, satisfied, satisfies speech. Speech, satisfied, satisfies Agni. Agni, satisfied, satisfies the earth. The earth, satisfied, satisfies whatever is covered by the earth, present, future, and past; it satisfies all that. He who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink, he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies.

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛptaḥ prāṇaṃ tarpayati | prāṇas tṛpto vāyuṃ tarpayati | vāyus tṛpta ākāśaṃ tarpayati | ākāśas tṛpto yat kiṃcākāśenāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: स तृप्तः प्राणं तर्पयति | प्राणस् तृप्तो वायुं तर्पयति | वायुस् तृप्त आकाशं तर्पयति | आकाशस् तृप्तो यत् किंचाकाशेनापिहितम् भवद् भविष्यद् भूतं तत् सर्वं तर्पयति | य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: He delighted delights breath, breath delighted delights wind, wind delighted delights ether, ether delighted all that is covered by ether. Present, future, past, all that he delights, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: He, satisfied, satisfies breath. Breath, satisfied, satisfies Vāyu. Vāyu, satisfied, satisfies space. Space, satisfied, satisfies whatever is covered by space, present, future, and past; it satisfies all that. He who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink, he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies.

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛptaś cakṣus tarpayati | cakṣus tṛptam ādityaṃ tarpayati | ādityas tṛpto divaṃ tarpayati |dyaus tṛptā yat kiṃcid divāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: स तृप्तश् चक्षुस् तर्पयति | चक्षुस् तृप्तम् आदित्यं तर्पयति | आदित्यस् तृप्तो दिवं तर्पयति |द्यौस् तृप्ता यत् किंचिद् दिवापिहितम् भवद् भविष्यद् भूतं तत् सर्वं तर्पयति | य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: He delighted delights the eye, the eye delighted delights the sun, the sun delighted delights the sky, the sky delighted whatever is covered by the sky. Present, future, past, all that he delights, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: He, satisfied, satisfies sight. Sight, satisfied, satisfies the sun. The sun, satisfied, satisfies heaven. Heaven, satisfied, satisfies whatever is covered by heaven, present, future, and past; it satisfies all that. He who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink, he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies.

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛpto manas tarpayati | manas tṛptaṃ candramasaṃ tarpayati | candramās tṛpto nakṣatrāṇi tarpayati | nakṣatrāṇi tṛptāni māsāṃs tarpayanti | māsās tṛptā ardhamāsāṃs tarpayanti | ardhamāsās tṛptā ahorātre tarpayanti | ahorātre tṛpte ṛtūṃs tarpayataḥ | ṛtavas tṛptāḥ saṃvatsaraṃ tarpayanti | saṃvatsaras tṛpto yat kiṃcit saṃvatsareṇāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: स तृप्तो मनस् तर्पयति | मनस् तृप्तं चन्द्रमसं तर्पयति | चन्द्रमास् तृप्तो नक्षत्राणि तर्पयति | नक्षत्राणि तृप्तानि मासांस् तर्पयन्ति | मासास् तृप्ता अर्धमासांस् तर्पयन्ति | अर्धमासास् तृप्ता अहोरात्रे तर्पयन्ति | अहोरात्रे तृप्ते ऋतूंस् तर्पयतः | ऋतवस् तृप्ताः संवत्सरं तर्पयन्ति | संवत्सरस् तृप्तो यत् किंचित् संवत्सरेणापिहितम् भवद् भविष्यद् भूतं तत् सर्वं तर्पयति | य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: He delighted delights the mind, the mind delighted delights the moon, the moon delighted delights the Naksatras, the Naksatras delighted delight the months, the months delighted delight the half-months, the half-months delighted delight the days and nights, the days and nights delighted delight the seasons, the seasons delighted delight the year, the year delighted whatever is covered by the year. Present, future, past, all that he delights, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: He, satisfied, satisfies the mind. The mind, satisfied, satisfies the moon. The moon, satisfied, satisfies the lunar mansions. The lunar mansions, satisfied, satisfy the months. The months, satisfied, satisfy the half-months. The half-months, satisfied, satisfy day and night. Day and night, satisfied, satisfy the seasons. The seasons, satisfied, satisfy the year. The year, satisfied, satisfies whatever is covered by the year, present, future, and past; it satisfies all that. He who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink, he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies.

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛptaḥ śrotraṃ tarpayati | śrotraṃ tṛptaṃ diśas tarpayati | diśas tṛptā avāntaradiśas tarpayanti | avāntaradiśas tṛptā yat kiṃcāvāntaradigbhir apihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: स तृप्तः श्रोत्रं तर्पयति | श्रोत्रं तृप्तं दिशस् तर्पयति | दिशस् तृप्ता अवान्तरदिशस् तर्पयन्ति | अवान्तरदिशस् तृप्ता यत् किंचावान्तरदिग्भिर् अपिहितम् भवद् भविष्यद् भूतं तत् सर्वं तर्पयति | य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: He delighted delights the ear, the ear delighted delights the quarters, the quarters delighted delight the intermediate quarters, the intermediate quarters what is covered by the intermediate quarters. Present, future, past, all that he delights, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: He, satisfied, satisfies hearing. Hearing, satisfied, satisfies the directions. The directions, satisfied, satisfy the intermediate directions. The intermediate directions, satisfied, satisfy whatever is covered by the intermediate directions, present, future, and past; it satisfies all that. He who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink, he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies.

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛpto retas tarpayati | retas tṛptam apas tarpayati | āpas tṛptā nadīṃs tarpayanti | nadyas tṛptāḥ samudraṃ tarpayanti | samudro tṛpto yat kiṃcit samudreṇāpihitam bhavad bhaviṣyad bhūtaṃ tat sarvaṃ tarpayati | ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca so 'śnāti sa pibati sa tṛpyati sa tarpayati ||
meaning: स तृप्तो रेतस् तर्पयति | रेतस् तृप्तम् अपस् तर्पयति | आपस् तृप्ता नदींस् तर्पयन्ति | नद्यस् तृप्ताः समुद्रं तर्पयन्ति | समुद्रो तृप्तो यत् किंचित् समुद्रेणापिहितम् भवद् भविष्यद् भूतं तत् सर्वं तर्पयति | य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च सो ऽश्नाति स पिबति स तृप्यति स तर्पयति ||
text: He delighted delights seed, seed delighted delights the waters, the waters delighted delight the rivers, the rivers delighted delight the ocean, the ocean delighted whatever is covered by the ocean. Present, future, past, all that he delights, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. He eats, he drinks, he delights, he causes delight.
text_mt: He, satisfied, satisfies semen. Semen, satisfied, satisfies the waters. The waters, satisfied, satisfy the rivers. The rivers, satisfied, satisfy the ocean. The ocean, satisfied, satisfies whatever is covered by the ocean, present, future, and past; it satisfies all that. He who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink, he eats, he drinks, he is satisfied, and he satisfies.

sanskrit_iast: sa tṛptas tad etad vairājaṃ daśavidhaṃ agnihotraṃ bhavati | tasya prāṇa evāhavanīyaḥ | apāno gārhapatyo vyāno 'nvāhāryapacano mano dhūmo manyur arcir dantā aṅgārāḥ śraddhā payo vāk samit satyam āhutiḥ prajñātmā sa rasaḥ | tad etad vairājaṃ daśavidhaṃ agnihotraṃ hutaṃ bhavati | rohobhyāṃ rohobhyām abhyārūḷham abhi svargaṃ lokaṃ gamayati ya evaṃ vidvān aśnāti ca pibati cāśayati ca pāyayati ca | atha ya idam avidvān agnihotraṃ juhoti yathāṅgārān apohya bhasmani hutaṃ tādṛk tatyās tādṛk tat syāt ||
meaning: स तृप्तस् तद् एतद् वैराजं दशविधं अग्निहोत्रं भवति | तस्य प्राण एवाहवनीयः | अपानो गार्हपत्यो व्यानो ऽन्वाहार्यपचनो मनो धूमो मन्युर् अर्चिर् दन्ता अङ्गाराः श्रद्धा पयो वाक् समित् सत्यम् आहुतिः प्रज्ञात्मा स रसः | तद् एतद् वैराजं दशविधं अग्निहोत्रं हुतं भवति | रोहोभ्यां रोहोभ्याम् अभ्यारूऌहम् अभि स्वर्गं लोकं गमयति य एवं विद्वान् अश्नाति च पिबति चाशयति च पाययति च | अथ य इदम् अविद्वान् अग्निहोत्रं जुहोति यथाङ्गारान् अपोह्य भस्मनि हुतं तादृक् तत्यास् तादृक् तत् स्यात् ||
text: He delighted is the tenfold, Yiraj-like, Agnihotra. His expiration is the Ahavanlya (fire), his inspiration the Giirhapatya, his Yyiina the Anvaharyapacana, his mind the smoke, his anger the flame, his teeth the coals, his faith the milk, his speech the brand, his truth the oblation, his intelligent self the essence. That Yiraj-like, tenfold, Agnihotra is offered. Him it sends to the world of heaven, which is mounted by these two ascents, who knowing this eats and drinks and makes to eat and drink. Now if one, knowing not this Agnihotra, sacrifices, it is with him as though he pushed aside the coals and made oblation in the ashes.
text_mt: He, satisfied—this is that ten-fold agnihotra belonging to the Virāj. Its āhavanīya fire is prāṇa; its gārhapatya fire is apāna; its anvāhāryapacana fire is vyāna; the mind is its smoke; anger is the flame; the teeth are the embers; faith is the milk; speech is the firewood; truth is the oblation; the conscious self is the essence. Thus this ten-fold agnihotra belonging to the Virāj is offered. Mounted step by step, it leads him to the heavenly world who, knowing thus, eats and drinks, feeds and gives to drink. But if one without this knowledge offers the agnihotra, it is just as if one were to push aside the embers and offer into ashes—such would that be, such would that be.

sanskrit_iast: prajāpatir vā imaṃ puruṣam udañcata | tasminn etā devatā āveśayad vācy agniṃ prāṇe vāyuṃ apāne vidyuta udāne parjanyaṃ cakṣuṣy ādityaṃ manasi candramasaṃ śrotre diśaḥ śarīre pṛthivīṃ retasy apo bala indraṃ manyāv īśānaṃ mūrdhany ākāśaṃ ātmani brahma | sa yathā mahān amṛtakumbhaḥ pinvamānas tiṣṭhed evaṃ haiva sa tasthau | atha hemā devatā īkṣāṃ cakrire kim ayam asmābhiḥ puruṣaḥ kariṣyati kiṃ vā vayam anena | hantāsmāc carīrād utkramāmeti | tā hoccakramuḥ | atha hedaṃ śarīraṃ riktam iva parisuṣiraṃ sa hekṣāñcakre prajāpatī randhrāya na kṣamam | hantāham imā aśanāyāpipāsābhyām upasṛjā iti | tā hopasasṛje | tā hopāṣrṣṭāḥ sukhaṃ alabhamānā imam eva puruṣaṃ punaḥ pratyāviviśuḥ ||
